cohort: 21,302 postpartum participants who visited Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital from September 2019 to February 2022
finding: Age, neonatal weight, vaginal delivery, episiotomy, and forceps delivery were risk factors for reduced pelvic floor muscle strength, while higher body mass index, parity (≤ 3) and gestational weight gain were associated with greater pelvic floor muscle strength.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was associated with greater pelvic floor muscle strength compared to vaginal delivery.
